distinction_from_round5: This fixes arbitrary nonzero C strictly inside its physical range and perturbs B around zero. C is not assumed small. The older theorem instead fixed interior (A,B) and required sufficiently small C.

definitions.model: p(x)=A+B cos(x)+C sin(x), B^2+C^2<=min(A,1-A)^2; take C>0 by reflection.
definitions.oracle: V(A,B,C)=sup_w inf_{physical(a,b)} integral kl(p(x)||a+b cos(x)) w(dx), with natural logarithms.
definitions.reflection_objective: R_B(z)=K(A+Bz,C sqrt(1-z^2)), z in[-1,1], with the continuous value0 at endpoints.
definitions.reflection_center: q_B(z)=Q(A+Bz,C sqrt(1-z^2)), continuously extended by q_B(+/-1)=A+/-B.

theorem.assumptions: Fix0<A<1 and0<C<min(A,1-A). There exists epsilon(A,C)>0 such that all |B|<epsilon satisfy physicality and the statements below.
theorem.unique_optimum: R_B has a unique interior maximizer z*(B), real analytic in B near0, with z*(0)=0.
theorem.exact_design: V(A,B,C)=R_B(z*(B)). The reflection angles +/-arccos(z*) with plus weight omega=[q_B(z*)-(A+Bz*-C sqrt(1-z*^2))]/[2C sqrt(1-z*^2)] attain it.
theorem.global_null_certificate: b*=partial_z q_B(z*), a*=q_B(z*)-b*z*. This physical affine null satisfies kl(p(x)||a*+b*cos(x))<=R_B(z*) for every real x.
theorem.one_sided_null: The same design/value hold when the null includes all physical sine coefficients C_null<=0; negative C follows by reflection.
theorem.scope: The neighborhood depends on the fixed(A,C); no uniform statement as C approaches0 or min(A,1-A), and no numeric epsilon is supplied.

proof.claim: The B=0 certificate is a strict global two-contact saddle.
proof.argument: Let q0=Q(A,C), K0=K(A,C)>0. The two rates A+/-C lie strictly in(0,1) and q0 is strictly between them. For every z!=0, both A+/-C sqrt(1-z^2) lie strictly between A-C and A+C. Strict convexity of p->kl(p||q0) and equality of its two endpoint values therefore give F_plus(z),F_minus(z)<K0; both reach K0 atz=0. Their second derivatives there are -C[logit(A+C)-logit(q0)]<0 and C[logit(A-C)-logit(q0)]<0, respectively.

proof.claim: The reflection capacity maximizer is nondegenerate.
proof.argument: With omega=(q0-A+C)/(2C), g_plus=logit(A+C)-logit(q0)>0 and g_minus=logit(A-C)-logit(q0)<0, the envelope derivative is K_C=omega*g_plus-(1-omega)*g_minus>0. AtB=0,z=0, partial_z R_0=0 and partial_zz R_0=-C*K_C<0. Since the constant null in Step1 has strictly smaller maximal KL away fromz=0, the capacity R_0 also has its unique global maximum atz=0.

proof.claim: The capacity maximum persists uniquely for small B.
proof.argument: Fixed C<min(A,1-A) supplies a uniform positive probability margin for sufficiently smallB. The symmetric entropy secant and capacity are analytic in the squared half-width c^2, includingc=0, so R_B and q_B are analytic in(B,z) around the compact strip B=0,z in[-1,1]. The implicit-function theorem at the nondegenerate maximum gives analytic z*(B). Choose a compact interval J around0 where R_0 has uniformly negative second derivative. LocalC2 convergence preserves strict concavity onJ; uniformC0 convergence and the strict gap on the compact complement of interior(J) exclude maximizers outsideJ. Thus the global maximizer is unique.

proof.claim: The tangent null remains physical and has two equal stationary contacts.
proof.argument: AtB=0 the center is q0 atz=0 and its z derivative is0. Hence(a*,b*) tends to(q0,0), strictly inside the physical affine-null region, so physicality persists. Atz* the tangent line matches q_B in value and first z derivative. Each branch F_plus/minus=kl(A+Bz+/-C sqrt(1-z^2)||a*+b*z) therefore equals R_B(z*) and has derivative partial_z R_B(z*)=0.

proof.claim: The two stationary contacts globally dominate the full circle.
proof.argument: Choose a smaller compact J around0 where the two B=0 branch second derivatives are uniformly negative; this is possible by Step1. OnJ, the perturbed branches converge in the C2 function norm, so they remain strictly concave and attain their unique maxima atz*. On K=[-1,1] minus interior(J), Step1 and compactness give a strictly positive gap belowK0 for both branches. Their uniformC0 convergence on[-1,1] and R_B(z*)->K0 preserve the gap for smallB. Thus F_plus/minus(z)<=R_B(z*) for everyz. This is a global domination proof, not merely a local stationary-point argument.

proof.claim: The design lower bound matches the global null upper bound.
proof.argument: At a reflected pair every C_null=0 affine null has one common rate. The chosen capacity weight makes that rate minimized at q_B(z*), with valueR_B(z*), and a constant physical null attains the minimum. Thus the design gives V>=R_B(z*). The physical tangent null from Step5 gives V<=R_B(z*) for every design, regardless of support size; it also rules out a better boundary null design indirectly through this global upper bound. No minimax exchange is assumed.

At the reflected pair, an opposite-sign null has q_plus<=q_minus while the true endpoints are strictly ordered the other way. Weighted Bernoulli-KL projection onto this order cone pools at the weighted mean q_B(z*), which the constant physical null attains. The same C_null=0 tangent line gives the upper certificate, completing the sandwich.

closed_local_expansions.notation: All Q,K and their A,C derivatives below are evaluated at the fixed(A,C), and all O constants depend on(A,C).
closed_local_expansions.symmetry: R_{-B}(-z)=R_B(z), so uniqueness implies z*(-B)=-z*(B), V(-B)=V(B), a*(-B)=a*(B), and b*(-B)=-b*(B).
closed_local_expansions.interpretation: The quadratic improvement relative to the B-independent PSR capacity K(A,C) is nonnegative. This is oracle information only; it is not a finite stopping-cost gain.
